title: Scripture equally bars works of the flesh from the kingdom
source_text: X. At vero haec eadem Scriptura non minus aperte & frequenter inculcat peccata illa graviora, quae vocat opera carnis, hominem regno coelorum excludere; nec qui ejusmodi peccata committit posse Deo placere, & regni ipsius haeredem fieri. Nolite errare, inquit Paulus, neque fornicarii, neque idolis servientes, neque adulteri, neque molles, neque masculorum concubitores, neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque maledici, neque rapaces regnum Dei possidebunt. Item, Manifesta sunt autem opera carnis, quae sunt adulterium, immunditia, impudicitia, luxuria, idolorum servitus, veneficia, inimicitiae, contentiones, aemulationes, irae, rixae, dissensiones, sectae, invidiae, homicidia, ebrietates, comessationes, & his similia, quae praedico vobis, sicut praedixi, quoniam qui talia agunt regnum Dei non consequentur. Unde non minus evidenter patet illos qui consueverunt istiusmodi flagitia patrare, & quos mors opprimit alicui illorum operam dantes, esse non posse salutis aeternae participes, ac proinde omnia ejusmodi peccata omnino pugnare cum sanctitate illa, cui vita & gloria aeterna promissa est; nec cum illis posse bonam conscientiam retineri, ac legitimam salutis aeternae fiduciam: sed quamdiu aliquis in ullo peccatorum istiusmodi manet, tamdiu mortis & perditionis aeternae reum teneri, non tantum juxta legis rigorem, sed quoque juxta ipsum Evangelii foedus. 1 Cor. 6. Gal. 5.
pass_a_gloss: But this same Scripture no less openly and frequently inculcates that those graver sins which it calls works of the flesh exclude a man from the kingdom of heaven; nor can he who commits such sins please God and become heir of his kingdom. Be not deceived, says Paul; neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners shall possess the kingdom of God. Likewise, Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are adultery, uncleanness, lasciviousness, luxury, idolatry, witchcrafts, enmities, contentions, emulations, wraths, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, envyings, murders, drunkennesses, revelings, and such like: of which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God. Whence it no less evidently appears that those who have been accustomed to commit such outrages, and whom death overtakes while they are giving themselves to any of them, cannot be partakers of eternal salvation; and therefore all such sins altogether fight with that holiness to which eternal life and glory are promised; nor with them can a good conscience be retained, and a lawful confidence of eternal salvation: but so long as anyone remains in any of such sins, so long he is held guilty of eternal death and perdition, not only according to the rigor of the law, but also according to the very covenant of the Gospel. 1 Cor. 6. Gal. 5.
pass_b_english: Paul’s catalogs of fleshly works shut their doers out of the kingdom—gospel covenant as well as law.
While someone stays in those crimes, good conscience and lawful assurance of salvation cannot hold.
